name: Widgeteer – AI Form Builder
author: nofusshere

sections.description:
Widgeteer is your agent marketeer and engineer. It doesn’t just create crisp marketing material such as FAQs and before-and-after sliders, it also builds fully working forms. Receive an instant email on every submission, or pass submissions on to Zapier, n8n and more. Countdown timer? Product feedback form? Product recommendation quiz? It does all that and more.

  • Create working forms, FAQ sections or “whatever” using AI.
  • All done for you: no setup, no keys needed. Join and generate.
  • No tech, no config, no code. This is our job, not yours.
  • Made in, and supported from, Britain 🇬🇧

What you can build

  • Contact, callback and appointment request forms
  • Newsletter and waiting-list sign-ups
  • Product feedback forms and recommendation quizzes
  • FAQ sections, countdown timers and before-and-after sliders
  • Restaurant menus, price lists and other content cards
  • Surveys, ratings and multi-step questionnaires

How it works

  1. Install and activate the plugin, then open Widgeteer in your dashboard menu.
  2. Enter your email address. We send you a one-time code, so there is no password to remember.
  3. Describe the widget you want, or pick an idea from the prompt library, and press Generate.
  4. Add it to any page with the Widgeteer AI Widget block, or paste its shortcode.
  5. Choose what happens when someone submits: an email to you, or a hand-off to Zapier, n8n and other tools.

Everything in one place

  • See every submission, and whether it was delivered, without leaving WordPress.
  • Match your brand with your own accent colour and font.
  • Works on single sites and on multisite networks.

Pricing

The plugin is free and nothing inside it is locked. Widgeteer itself is a hosted service, and what you can do each month depends on your plan with that service.

Free

  • 3 widgets
  • 2 actions or integrations
  • 100 submissions per month

Premium, $8.70 per month

  • 50 widgets
  • 10 actions or integrations
  • Unlimited submissions
  • Fan-making support

Plan limits are applied by the Widgeteer service, not by the plugin. Upgrading from inside the plugin arrives in a coming update.

External services

Widgeteer is a hosted service, and this plugin connects your site to it. The plugin cannot work without it.

What is sent to Widgeteer (https://app.widgeteer.ai)

  • Your email address and one-time code, when you sign in. The sign-in token you get back is stored encrypted on your site.
  • Your description of the widget, your colour and font choices and the address your site receives submissions on, when you generate a widget.
  • The fields a visitor fills in, when they submit a widget form, so the service can deliver them (for example by email or to a connected tool).
  • Requests for your widgets, actions and activity, when you open those screens.

What visitors’ browsers load (https://cdn.widgeteer.ai)

  • Each widget, and the script and styles that display it, are loaded from the Widgeteer CDN when a page containing a widget is viewed. The same happens in the editor and the plugin’s preview. As with any web request, the CDN sees the visitor’s IP address, browser and the address of the page. No form contents are sent in those requests.

The service is operated by Widgeteer. Terms of service: https://widgeteer.ai/terms/. Privacy policy: https://widgeteer.ai/privacy-policy.

Development

The plugin’s admin screens are built from the source files in the resources/ folder using Vite. To rebuild them, run npm install and then npm run build. The third-party libraries they include (Vue, Vue Router, Element Plus and lodash) are listed in package.json.
sections.faq:
Do I need an account?

Yes. You create one inside the plugin with just your email address, and we email you a one-time code to sign in.

Is it free?

The plugin is free. The Widgeteer service it connects to has a free plan and a paid plan, described under Pricing.

Do I need to know how to code?

No. Describe what you want in plain English and Widgeteer builds it for you.

How do I add a widget to a page?

In the block editor, add the Widgeteer AI Widget block and pick your widget. Anywhere else, paste the shortcode shown on the widget’s page, for example [widgeteer_widget id="123"].

Where do form submissions go?

To your Widgeteer account, which emails you or passes them on to the tools you connected. You can review them under Widgeteer → Activity. They are not stored in your WordPress database.

What happens if I delete the plugin?

Its settings and data are removed from your site. Your Widgeteer account and your widgets are kept, so you can reinstall and sign in again at any time.
